description:
Ur Genesis is an Iraqi team inspired by Mesopotamia, driven by science, technology, creativity, and exploration.

From the cradle of civilization to the frontier of space. 🚀🇮🇶
summary: UR-Genesis is an interactive digital storytelling web application developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, dedicated to commemorating NASA's legendary Mars Opportunity rover. The project addresses the mission challenge by transforming complex space exploration data and historical milestones into an immersive, user-friendly web experience. Designed with a sleek aesthetic and bilingual support (English and Arabic), UR-Genesis features an interactive mission timeline, detailed robotic component breakdowns, atmospheric simulation elements such as dust storm conditions, and engaging educational narratives. This project is vital because it bridges the gap between deep space science and public engagement, preserving the inspiring legacy of humanity's most successful Martian robotic missions for future explorers and school-age learners
details:
What it does & How it works: UR-Genesis is an interactive digital storytelling web application that follows two characters (Amar and Inanna) on a narrative journey connecting ancient Mesopotamia to the Mars Opportunity rover mission. Users can explore a 12-part story, real mission facts, an interactive quiz, NASA tool resources, and a Martian dust storm simulation.
Benefits & Intended Impact: It educates school-age learners and the general public about planetary exploration in an engaging, narrative-driven format, increasing long-term retention of scientific facts and keeping Opportunity's memory alive.
Tools Used: Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages, with descriptive content and code structuring assisted by Claude, and fact-checking and narrative refinement supported by ChatGPT and Gemini.
Creativity: The project uniquely blends ancient cultural storytelling with modern planetary science.
Factors Considered: Accessibility, bilingual UI (English/Arabic), responsive mobile-desktop design, and strict scientific accuracy based on official NASA data were core factors considered by our Iraqi team.
